name: Bitcoin USD
oneLiner: BtcUSD is BTCfi's overcollateralized USD stablecoin minted from BTC variants (WBTC, BTCB, cbBTC, native BTC) via Liquity-style CDP vaults.
collateral: Overcollateralized Bitcoin (WBTC, BTCB, cbBTC, native BTC) via CDP vaults

oracleRisk.summary: BtcUSD is a BiFi-style multi-handler CDP on Bifrost: market manager 0xd7b21280 prices each collateral handler through oracle proxy 0x6853f777, which maps handlers to Bifrost native Chainlink-compatible USD feeds (WBTC/USD, BTCB/USD, BTC/USD). Borrow limit is 50% LTV and margin-call limits are 95% (99.9% for BTCB); liquidations are third-party partial liquidations with an owner circuit breaker, no liquidation delay or auction window on any handler, and no secondary-feed failover.

branchApplicability.rationale: BTCFi's getAvailableBtcfiHandlers API and identical-bytecode Bifrost handlers enumerate four collateral markets (WBTC, BTCB, BTC, cbBTC) plus the BtcUSD debt handler. On-chain at Bifrost block 37135464, oracle proxy getOracleFeed(handlerId) returns distinct feed addresses for WBTC and BTCB and a shared BTC/USD feed for native BTC and cbBTC, while getTokenHandlerBorrowLimit/MarginCallLimit differ by handler (BTCB margin-call 99.9% vs 95% elsewhere). Market-specific feed and liquidation-parameter branches are therefore required.

branches.label: WBTC collateral handler
branches.summary: Handler 0 (WBTC) is priced by Bifrost native WBTC/USD feed 0xc1596ece via oracle proxy 0x6853f777; 50% borrow limit and 95% margin-call limit; proxy uses latestAnswer only with zero-price revert and no secondary feed.
branches.fallbackBehavior: Oracle proxy getTokenPrice calls feed.latestAnswer only (BiFi oracleProxy.sol); reverts on zero price; no last-good-price cache and no secondary feed. Owner 0xf357a08c can setOracleFeed/setOracleProxy.

collateralParameters.note: On-chain getTokenHandlerBorrowLimit(0)=0.5e18 (50% LTV); mint docs state maximum 50% of collateral. Margin-call/liquidation threshold getTokenHandlerMarginCallLimit(0)=0.95e18 (liquidatable when borrow >= 95% of deposit value).

branches.liquidationMechanism: BiFi-style third-party partialLiquidation when aggregate borrow >= sum(deposit*marginCallLimit); liquidator repays BtcUSD and receives collateral reward via market manager. No delay, grace period, auction window, or bidding queue exists on that path: liquidationManager.partialLiquidation carries only the circuitBreaker modifier, and its eligibility test _checkLiquidation is an instantaneous comparison of current oracle-priced deposit and borrow balances with no timestamp or block-height term. Proved callable at Bifrost block 37501309 (2026-08-09): market manager 0xd7b2128083ffc91a05d77cc90c7a34f8dac59de5 getCircuitBreaker() is false, getTokenHandlerSupport(0) is 1, and partialLiquidationUser reverts Error("LM") for an unauthorized caller while an authorized caller passes every authority check and reaches the collateral arithmetic (Error("unified div by zero") against an empty test position) — no timer stands between the two.
branches.backstop: No stability pool or protocol-owned backstop identified; recovery depends on external liquidators.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Market manager getCircuitBreaker() was false at observation; owner can freeze handlers via circuit breaker. Zero feed answer reverts pricing. No automatic bad-debt socialization or branch isolation beyond the shared circuit breaker was identified.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At Base block 48644528, the BtcUSD proxy points to verified ERC20_Bridged implementation 0x6e9070b8a8dbbc6cad6b6d029a5c6f6a653b74a9 and is unpaused. Its source gives every owner or admin authority to call set_blacklists(address[], bool), and transfer hooks reject both blacklisted senders and recipients; set_pause(bool) stops all token transfers. Current owners are 0x26FcE52a077b4f1dbD7C920b6f23a1D9d18DdDbE and 0xf98e8601A1eEF3BCE943f9B002e83Db8a0951Aa5, and current admin is 0x4F7aB59b5AC112970F5dD66D8a7ac505c8E5e08B; the latter owner successfully simulated both control calls through the proxy without broadcasting state. At Bifrost block 36763950, native BtcUSD reports paused=false, owner/defaultAdmin 0xa4247099c1462f9D9121a1809D001c1a6cC70dD5 has DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, and the runtime exposes pause/unpause; an unprivileged pause call reverts for the missing default-admin role. The Bifrost explorer did not expose verified source or ABI, so this does not assert native blacklist semantics, but both deployments have direct holder-transfer restriction surfaces.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 access review

mintAuthority.summary: BtcUSD's canonical Bifrost issuance runs through the BTCFi BtcUSD CDP handler 0x682143652b6e305730dd12b0dc7c38d5048fb647, a non-proxy contract that holds the token's keccak("Minter") role and mints against deposited BTC-variant collateral; the token's DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE EOA can grant or revoke that role but cannot mint directly. On Base, the ERC20_Bridged proxy's two owners mint the bridged representation, and its proxy admin resolves to an EOA. The Bifrost AccessControl is non-enumerable and public Bifrost RPCs cannot serve full-history role-grant logs, so membership exclusivity and the unverified Base owner contract cap this review at manual-review.

controls.evidence: 2026-07-20 via the Bifrost public EVM RPC: the native BtcUSD token 0x6906ccda405926fc3f04240187dd4fad5df6d555 is a 13.9KB non-proxy contract whose owner() returns this EOA (no contract code). eth_call to mint(address,uint256) from this owner reverted AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount, so it is not a direct minter. However, hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, owner) returned true, getRoleAdmin(MINTER_ROLE) returned DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, and eth_call to grantRole(MINTER_ROLE, owner) from this owner succeeded. It can therefore authorize minters, while current MINTER_ROLE membership remains unenumerable because getRoleMemberCount reverts and the token source/CDP controller is unverified.

controls.label: BTCFi BtcUSD CDP handler (native minter)
controls.capDescription: The handler mints BtcUSD only through the BTCFi CDP borrow path against deposited BTC-variant collateral, bounded by collateral balances, the 50% maximum LTV, and oracle pricing; it holds no role-admin capability.
controls.evidence: BTCFi's own getAvailableBtcfiHandlers API identifies this contract (chainId 3068) as the BtcUSD token handler. At Bifrost block 37087890 (2026-07-27): hasRole(keccak256("Minter") = 0x6e58ad548d72b425ea94c15f453bf26caddb061d82b2551db7fdd3cefe0e9940, this contract) returned true on the native BtcUSD token, and an eth_call simulation of mint(address,uint256) from this address succeeded while identical simulations from the token owner EOA and the four collateral handler contracts reverted with AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount(account, Minter). The handler is a 5,266-byte non-proxy contract (EIP-1967 implementation slot zero, no owner()).

controls.label: BtcUSD Base bridge owner contract
controls.evidence: At Base block 48621895, get_owners() on the ERC20_Bridged token returned this contract as one of two current owners. The verified bridge implementation permits token owners to mint bridged BtcUSD directly; the owner contract is not verified as a Safe or bounded multisig.

controls.label: BtcUSD Base bridge owner EOA
controls.evidence: At Base block 48621895, get_owners() on the ERC20_Bridged token returned this EOA as one of two current owners. The verified bridge implementation permits token owners to mint bridged BtcUSD directly.

controls.label: BtcUSD Base proxy admin (unverified contract)
controls.evidence: At Base block 48621895, the EIP-1967 admin slot of the BtcUSD bridge proxy returned this deployed contract and the implementation slot returned 0x6e9070b8. 2026-07-20 follow-up: the admin is a 10.25KB contract whose slot-0 owner reads as EOA 0xf9d5bd4013c955175185e406b407d5cee90b0001 (no contract code), so the upgrade authority chain resolves to that EOA; the admin contract itself remains source-unverified, so its delay and signer policy are unknown.

review.evidence: At Base block 48621895, BtcUSD is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy with enumerable direct bridge-token mint owners 0x26fce52a and 0xf98e8601. The Base proxy admin and its slot-0 EOA owner are also identified. On Bifrost, native BtcUSD owner() returns 0xa4247099c1462f9d9121a1809d001c1a6cc70dd5; it is the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE holder and can grant the mint role, but cannot mint directly. Follow-up at Bifrost block 37087890 (2026-07-27): the token's mint gate is keccak256("Minter") (not OZ's MINTER_ROLE — getRoleMemberCount reverts because the token uses plain, non-enumerable AccessControl). BTCFi's own handler API names 0x682143652b6e305730dd12b0dc7c38d5048fb647 as the BtcUSD token handler; hasRole(Minter, handler) returned true and a mint simulation from the handler succeeded, while simulations from the owner EOA and all four collateral handlers reverted AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount. The handler is a non-proxy 5,266-byte contract, so the canonical CDP mint path is resolved. Two limits cap confidence at manual-review: (1) plain AccessControl membership cannot be enumerated without grant-event history, and both public Bifrost RPC families (public-01/02.mainnet.bifrostnetwork.com, public-01/02.mainnet.thebifrost.io) time out on getLogs beyond single-block ranges, so a second Minter member cannot be excluded on-chain; (2) the Base bridge owner contract 0x26fce52a077b4f1dbd7c920b6f23a1d9d18dddbe is source-unverified on Blockscout/Basescan/Sourcify and exposes no Safe or owner() interface (getOwners/getThreshold/owner all return empty), so its internal signer policy is unknown. M-2 evidence review 2026-08-08: reconciliation downgraded continuous -> unknown - the review evidences the mint-role topology (bridge-token owners, handler role) but states no mechanism reconciling BtcUSD supply against BTC backing, no reserve endpoint is sourced, and no artefact names what is reconciled against what. The unbounded-reconciled posture's reconciled leg is therefore unsupported; V9 grades it conservatively while reconciliation is unknown.
review.reviewer: P2 mint-free cohort; Kimi data review

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: BtcUSD/BTCFi relies on Bifrost cross-chain technology for collateral movement across networks. Bifrost bridge documentation describes a cross-chain bridge service rather than a native issuer-only route, so Pharos scores this as external validated-network exposure.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex bridge route review; Kimi P2 control cohort dc-5 (lead usd1-world-liberty-financial)

reserveReview.rationale: The configured BTCFi producer reports the current collateral mix by supported handler. Native BTC is direct crypto collateral, while BTCB, cbBTC, and WBTC retain their wrapper issuer, custody, counterparty, and smart-contract failure domains.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: BTCFi current collateral balances by supported handler, refreshed 2026-08-09 from the BTCFi market API (deposit_value BTC 3,870,695.66 / BTCB 2,881,579.40 / cbBTC 74,635.15 / WBTC 4,702.87 of the $6,831,613.08 covered by the supported-handler registry) and normalized over the handlers the producer can see
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The four handlers above are the full set the BTCFi supported-handler API publishes (ids 0-4, of which id 2 is the BtcUSD borrow side), and their wrapper custody and redemption risks remain explicit structured risk factors. On 2026-08-09 the BTCFi market API additionally returned a handler id 5 holding 133,780,914.2 units worth $847,661.29 (about 11% of true collateral, priced at 0.00633619 and identified on-chain as a JPYC collateral handler on Bifrost) that the supported-handler registry does not list, so the producer cannot see it and it is not represented in the composition above.
